notes.title: iGrow Game is 10 years old!
notes.content:
Hi All,

It has been awhile, I know. Unbelievably it's been 10 years after the initial launch of this game and years away from this project consuming my life. I always hoped I would one day be able to pick iGrow Game up again and work on it. However that never happened and now it isn't possible. I don't think I still have all of the source for the game and the engine is entirely gone from the web so I can't even download the engine any more.

It has come to my attention that the game might be having issues with new versions of operating systems. I can't confirm this as I'm yet to test myself but I do believe the game was launched on windows 10 so it could be other reasons causing this. However I recommend changing the compatibility settings of the .exe to something like windows 7 to be sure. I will try and help anyone experiencing these issues if you will work with me to try and get to the bottom of it. However there isn't likely a fix I'm able to implement, because I'm unable to make a new build of the game and this is also certainly due to the game engine which is completely abandoned, so that isn't going to ever be fixed in an update.

Recently a few have expressed their disappointment with me and the game as a whole due to bugs and crashes in their reviews. Understandable. The game isn't a AAA game built in 2024 by a large studio. The development was actually started around 2011 in an abandoned engine. The game was built entirely by myself as a passion project. I did not expect the popularity this game received and I tried my best with it. I've been criticised for not hiring a team to make the game. However that was never financially possible. I've been criticised for not adding weed emoticons, which steam would not allow me to do at the time (I tried). Seems like they have changed their attitude now. I've been criticised for the bugs and issues not being fixed. Other then the game breaking bug of physx needing a restart of your machine (completely out of my control) there were no other game breaking bugs in the game when I made the last update. Yes, small and annoying bugs that I spent 100's of hours attempting to fix. The testing, development and bug fixes were made difficult due to the design of the engine. I do believe most of the bugs are either obscure (hard to repeat) or out of my control (corrupt saves). I attempted to recode the saving but failed after many hours due to the design being implemented throughout the game, yes it was a bad design decision for sure but the game originally used a server which I had bigger ambitions for. Needing to sync with the server the saves are constant but in the end needed a single save function to avoid corruption. Following the in game advice on closing the game properly should avoid corrupted saves (which can be fixed in most cases as explained here: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1177371382).

However, despite the negativity from some. It's been over looked that the median time playing this game by all players has been 7 hours. Yes this game isn't going to be updated again. Yes this game has issues (some more annoying then others) but most players are playing this game for 7 hours. Some players have played 100's of hours. For all the frustration of some, this game has been enjoyed by so many and continue to do so. So I won't remove the game like some suggest and it will be continued to be sold. However always try the demo version out (that's why it is there) to make sure you won't have issues before purchasing. You will likely get more fun out of the game for your 79p then you would for most things you pay for every day for far more money.

More importantly, I had a wonderful experience with everyone who believed in the game and enjoyed it. It blew my expectations out of the water on how well this would be received. Especially considering all of the issues that happened along the way. This game is still one of my proudest achievements. It will always be and has also become a part of gaming history (a small part).

However, I have hung my hat up on the game and development has stopped for reasons out of my control. I pushed the engine to its limits and took the game as far as I could. It became unbearable to work on due to the process (I explain a lot more on the reply to this review https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198030784015/recommended/489020/#developer_response).

That is the end of iGrow Game's development and after 10 years from release that took a huge chunk of my life being dedicated to it. That does not mean the idea has finished. iGrow Game is unique and still is. It's a crime simulator as much as it is a weed growing game and that isn't a subject matter really any other game explores like iGrow Game does. It's dark, it's seedy and that's what it always was meant to be. I have not just considered a second game in the series. I even started development in a new engine. Something I would of liked to keep secret as I always try to do with my developments (takes the pressure off me) but I want to make it clear I haven't forgotten about you or iGrow Game. I also don't have the time I once had as I have a family now. So don't run away with this as I haven't worked on it for a year. If it happens, it happens.

I am here to help out with the issues and have unfortunately neglected you guys in the forum for a fair few years. Which I am sorry about, life has been very busy. This game burned me out so badly I gave up game development on larger projects altogether and switched to smaller web games instead.

If you have anything you want to ask me or mention. Please do so.

Thanks,
iDev

notes.title: Super Sale (83% off) + Suggest a strain!
notes.content:
It's a super sale! For 3 days only iGrow Game will be 83% off!

Though first off let me apologize for the lack of updates over the past few months. I worked pretty heavily on iGrow Game with a load of updates and pretty much burned myself out, being a game I work on in my free time single handedly. Which being a web developer in my full time job means changing my coding language and work flow every night to work on iGrow Game which is no easy task.

That being said, i monitor the game and part of the reason I stopped development was that the reports of bugs remaining in the game were no longer common or even that many, especially not game breaking. Like any game, there could always be more, but there is hours of gameplay already in the game and for the price tag I personally think its worth the money.

So I decided to spend my time on my other main project that desperately needed some attention:
https://play.idevgames.co.uk

play.idevgames.co.uk is my html5 web game platform made by a game developer for game developers! So if you want to support some really amazing game developers play their games for free and check the site out. Also my small HTML5 games are on there too.

Also that has led to creating a platform to help developers, publishers and gamers earn some money when sharing gaming related content online.
https://my-ga.me

my-ga.me is a URL shortener specifically for shortening links to gaming related content. So if you often post about gaming on facebook, twitter, reddit etc... its worth a try. Also all of the above is free and aims to help indie game developers who want to bring you awsome imaginative games like iGrow Game!

That being said, iGrow game isn't dead its just on hold for a bit. So to celebrate another sale I would like to add a few more strains to the game. So like I did before here: 
http://steamcommunity.com/games/489020/announcements/detail/468780659743124983

Feel free to suggest a strain in the comments!

Happy Growing!
-iDev

notes.title: HAPPY 420!
notes.content:
Well it's been almost a year since I launched iGrow Game on steam and before that it had been released on itch.io for about a year and a half. Not only is 420 the main holiday in the cannabis community, it also seems to be a milestone in the life of iGrow Game.

It all started one 420...

Well ok not quite! I'm not sure how it all started any more, it became just one of many projects at one point. I did abandon the game entirely at one point too when I came to actually coding the plant growing algorithm. Though after the 3rd total rewrite and 1000's of line's of code later. I managed to make something that appeared to work... Though actually was instead, very very broken. I worked myself thin and completely despised iGrow Game by this point but released it on itch.io anyway without properly testing anything. The game wasn't even playable until I got close to the point of releasing it either, so I never even played my own game other then testing as I went along! Anyways months, maybe a year later I finally looked back at it again and saw hope this time.

Actually this leads into the 420 part which is how iGrow Game's steam journey began at least. I noticed some youtubers had played the game and released videos. Of coarse one of them burned the game down to the ground for the broken mess it was at the time but the other youtuber (Chills504) didn't! He made light of the bugs and actually had some good things to say about the game. This inspired me to fix the game breaking bugs and push for a steam release and reach out to Chills504. 

Since then me and chills504 stay in touch and help each other out where we can. So I would like to say thank you to Chills504 for inspiring me to carry on! 

That all being said I didn't just want to wish everyone a happy 420. I also wanted to take this opportunity to thank every single person who has purchased iGrow Game, left me a nice comment, supported the game and of coarse everyone at steam for letting this be a reality!

I've talked to some amazing people from all over the world because of iGrow game. In my eyes this first year on steam has been a great success and I'll work harder to make the next one even more of a success! I'm no where near leaving my day job but the fact that something I designed and developed has been purchased by 50 shy of 5000, is truly amazing! Someone from nearly every country in the world has purchased a copy of iGrow game and that is really crazy to think!

So thank you all for supporting the future of iGrow game, please stay tuned for more, I'm definitely not finished yet. Have a great 420 and stay safe no matter what it is you'll be doing.

As always...

Happy Growing!
-iDev

notes.title: v1.32 Room Control
notes.content:
So after a fair few bug fixes I felt it was time to focus some time on a feature. I had a bright idea so I had to test it out. It turned out to be a really good idea. 

One thing a few people have mentioned was the struggle in running around maintaining your plants. So I came up with an idea I've decided to call room control.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25303165/3a9821890b4353a63adeb4ebe5ca52d6dbdd497c.png[/img]

Room control gives you the ability to maintain your room through a fixed top down camera view. Allowing you to click the points in the room making the whole process of growing a lot quicker.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25303165/7c9aa3cfc70c6955f2956c491c8bd55c33977325.png[/img]

It brings a whole new way to play the game and I have no dout this is one feature many players will be using most from now on.

There is a few bugs currently that I know of which I will fix in the coming week. I wanted to get this in your hands now so I've worked hard to get it finished. If you find any bugs don't forget to report them in case I don't know about them.

Let me know what you all think.

Happy Growing!
-iDev

notes.title: v1.3 You'll need ventilation if you don't want a raid
notes.content:
It's a big feature I've been working on for awhile. Luckily, it's finally finished! Ever since adding the "Needs" mechanics in the game I had this idea in mind and had started implementing it. Personally, I never liked the "Needs" mechanics. Actually that's why I made it an option. The ventilation mechanic isn't an option, it's now part of the game as I feel it add's to the realism.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25303165/e280a21715c55fd2df33edd0561ba10175114168.png[/img]

You can't let air be stale in your grow rooms, so to counter act this you will need to have a ventilation system. If you don't have one you will be raided as soon as you start growing. Not only that, you will also need to keep replacing your filters. Once you hit level 30 you will unlock filters that will not need replacing but it does come at a price.

Unfortunately I ran out of time and wasn't able to do any bug fixes this update but I assure you that I will focus entirely on bug fixes in the next updates. I had to finish this feature before looking into bug's as I was too far into this feature to release an update without it finished.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25303165/f94fe528c0292940aafcaff257cc162344286f19.png[/img]

I also wanted to thank everyone for your support for iGrow Game and keep an eye out for more updates very soon. Also if you have any problems or hit any bugs, please consider leaving your feedback in the forums as it will help me fix them if I know about them.

Happy Growing!
-iDev

notes.title: v1.25 Brings more choice and shine
notes.content:
I'm now becoming confident that iGrow Game is now solid, with no problems mentioned from anyone since the last update (fingers crossed). I've decided to focus on something I mentioned before. 

I wanted to bring some more room designs in game.

notes.title: v 1.245 - a fix patch
notes.content:
Ok unfortunately I've had a few problems recently. Some how I broke the game in several places from things i've done. So I reverted back to an earlier version on steam.

So I've had to spend some time adding all the latest fixes back in and attempting to fix new problems I've found. I've done a fair bit of testing and everything now seems stable and working like it should.

Like I mentioned before I have been trying to also fix the NaN bug that can happen sometimes. It's basically because the game get's closed while writing to disk. So no data gets saved. So now the game save's less and prompts you when it's saving. Also it won't allow you to exit the game from the menu's when saving. So hopefully unless you close the game from force closing you shouldn't have the NaN error again.

With this new update as well as 50% off during the steam winter sale. It's a great time to get the game and support future development.

If you do experience anything let me know in the forums. As soon as the game is stable I can think about adding more content.

Happy Growing
-iDev

notes.title: It's a Christmas Miracle!
notes.content:
A small Christmas update has (by accident) led to something big, a miracle actually! 

So let's start with that small Christmas update:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25303165/169d1eca21983da856b28459f4eb937e13f16163.png[/img]

This new strain is a cheeky Christmas inspired strain you can grow at level 17! Not for a limited time or anything, just my way of saying happy Christmas!

So, making a new strain was a good way to delve back under the hood of iGrow game and become familier with the code. Believe it or not, despite iGrow game looking simple on the surface. There's far more work to it then you would think and simple sounding jobs such as saving a game is monsterous systems alone. That being said it got me back into the swing of things and what I added is something I designed this game for from the beginning. 

Cross breeding strains!
It's in! And now this add's not just replayability it also pushs unlockables all the way to level 50! That's quite a jump from level 16. Not just that, this means you don't just have 39 (including the new Christmas strain) you will have over 1000 combinations to grow! Thats a huge jump! 

iGrow game isn't dead yet, I hope to get more work done over the holidays!

Happy Growing
-iDev

notes.title: v1.22 You've been raided!
notes.content:
A few players have suggested random raids to occur in the game. After a long time thinking of a way to work this into the game so they weren't just random. I've hopefully also created a new gameplay mechanic which will give you more to keep an eye on.

You now have a food, water and energy bars. You are able to buy from the vending machines in the lobby as well as sleep using the sleeping bag in the rooms.

If you let your food, water or energy bars hit 0 you will "Pass out" which means you get busted. If you are in the lobby you will lose all your inventory. If you don't keep an eye on these and you pass out in your room you will lose everything in the room, your inventory and £1000 fine.

This will also stop you from just keeping the speed on x10. I know this all might sound a bit strange at the moment but I'm hoping to expand on these mechanics. Hopefully this added feature improves the game. Maybe it's a terrible idea and you hate it. Let me know on the forums http://forum.igrowgame.co.uk/

Happy Growing
- iDev

notes.title: New update now available v1.21!
notes.content:
I've had some great feedback for iGrow Game over the past week. So I set to work on a new update. This is a quick run down of what's new to the game:

Light Height
The lights now automatically change height at certain points of the grow. It doesn't change the gamely in anyway but visually it adds more immersion.

Light Cycles
When the plant's start budding the cycle of the plant changes. This change is so subtle and won't even be noticeable until your able to grow some of the top strains that take longer to grow.

Game difficulty
One of the problems players have found is that it is just too easy to progress through the game. It should now take longer now giving a longer play through.

Crouch
With light movements I decided it would be a good idea to add the ability to crouch while in a room. Making it easier to access plants.

FOV
Field of view was an issue, should look right now.

DOF
Depth of field graphically takes the sharpness away from objects further away. There was none before but it is there now. I haven't added settings for FOV and DOF yet.

Many other minor fixes and changes has happened as well over the past week, including character movement tweaking. This is the beginning of many more updates hopefully. Want to see your suggestions in game then tell me about them on the forums http://forum.igrowgame.co.uk

Happy Growing!

- iDev

notes.title: Can Not Move? You Need PhysX!
notes.content:
It finally clicked, after a rewrite of the controls in the game and deciding the code was working fine. It hit me, it's the physics!

iGrow Game uses PhysX and it should now download automatically when launching the game the first time.

Incase it doesn't you can download it here:
http://www.nvidia.com/object/physx-9.15.0428-driver.html

Happy Growing!
- iDev

notes.title: Had a problem? look here!
notes.content:
Let me first say thank you all so much for an amazing launch. iGrow Game has been a labor of love which began in 2013! That's a fair few years of dreaming of how launching iGrow Game on steam would be. Before getting into the serous part of this announcement, I would like to start off by giving you a bit of information about iGrow Game. 

I am the only developer of iGrow Game (which explains some of the shoddy texturing and bad looking models). It can be incredibly difficult to make a game like this single handedly. It's almost impossible to perfect everything, though I have tried my best. I've really enjoyed seeing some players put in some hours and even unlock everything in the game! I've also been trying my best to fix the problem of moving some players are receiving.

I wanted to make this announcement especially for those having problems with loading. Luckily SepticSpoon was able to figure out if you disable "Legacy graphics mode" in the settings menu. This should fix the loading freeze.

As for the moving problem some are having. I'm working on it!

I also wanted to let you all know, I do plan on adding to the game. It's like many have said, it does what it's meant to do. Grow, harvest, sell and expand. Once I have sorted out these few bugs my aim is to add more functionality.

So if you have a problem or you need help. Don't leave a bad review, find me on the forums http://forum.igrowgame.co.uk or post in the community discussions. 

Thank you all and happy growing!
- iDev
